newsitem.title: USA: California controller convenes welfare commission.
newsitem.headline: California controller convenes welfare commission.

text.p: California state Controller Kathleen Connell on Tuesday convened the first meeting of a commission formed to help the state cope with federal welfare reform.

"California must show leadership in identifying job opportunities for the tens of thousands of people who must transition from the dependent state of welfare to an independent, self-supporting position in the job market," Connell said in a statement.
Connell said welfare reform would have far-reaching consequences for the state's economy, budget and tax revenues.
"The challenge met successfully will increase productivity and promote an expanded economy," Connell said. "Failure may well reverse California's recovery and limit its future economic growth."

The 25-member Work Opportunity Response Commission, made up of business, labor and county and state government leaders, was divided into committees that will focus on ways to move people from welfare to work.
The commission will focus on job training as well as on tax policies and incentives to encourage businesses to employ people leaving the welfare rolls.
Connell said her task force would work in conjunction with the Clinton administration.
Connell said moving people from welfare to work was "the single most important fiscal issue facing California."

Under federal welfare reform, federal spending would be reduced mainly by cutting food stamps aid and denying federal benefits to most legal immigrants. The reforms impose other limits on welfare benefits.
